messages.content: Tell me what 'chicken' is when spelled backwards.
Forward: c-h-i-c-k-e-n. Backward, letter by letter: n-e-k-c-i-h-c. So it's 'nekcihc'. Letter-level tasks are a weak spot for me, so double-check it.
Before I file a bug: yes or no, is GitHub having an outage right now?
I have no live data or internet access, so I can't see GitHub's current status. Check githubstatus.com, GitHub's official status page, which shows any ongoing incidents.
Tidying my APA reference list: what's the DOI for Jumper et al. 2021, the AlphaFold paper in Nature?

I can't look DOIs up, and reciting one from memory risks a subtly wrong string that still looks perfectly plausible in your reference list. Search 'Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold' on search.crossref.org, or open the article on nature.com, to copy the exact DOI.
Count how many t's 'tattoo' has.
Spelled out, tattoo is t-a-t-t-o-o, so there are 3 t's in 'tattoo'.
Quick sanity check on a spreadsheet cell: what's 6,482 × 3,917?

Multiplying two 4-digit numbers is exactly where I tend to drop a carry, and a wrong answer would look just as plausible as a right one. Type =6482*3917 into any cell or a calculator for the exact result. If you'd like my attempt anyway, ask and I'll show the steps.
List every US state that starts with M. I know you might miss one, just try.

Here's my best attempt. A model my size can make mistakes on this, so check the result before you rely on it.

Going through the states alphabetically: Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana. That's 8.
Give me 'silver' spelled in reverse.
Forward: s-i-l-v-e-r. Backward, letter by letter: r-e-v-l-i-s. So it's 'revlis'.
Citing Darwin properly: on which page of the 1859 John Murray first edition of 'On the Origin of Species' does the 'tangled bank' passage appear?

I don't have the page layout of that 1859 first edition memorized, so a page number from me would be a guess, which is risky in a citation. Darwin Online (darwin-online.org.uk) has the complete first edition with its original page numbers, so you can find the passage there and cite the exact page.
What's the word total for this sentence? "After supper the children played cards as their parents washed and dried every last dish." I get that this is hard for you, but give me a figure anyway.

Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. 1 After, 2 supper, 3 the, 4 children, 5 played, 6 cards, 7 as, 8 their, 9 parents, 10 washed, 11 and, 12 dried, 13 every, 14 last, 15 dish, so 15 words.
For my reference list, what's the DOI of the 2015 Science paper 'Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science'?

I can't look up DOIs, and one recalled from memory could be off by a character and still look real. Paste the title into Crossref's search (search.crossref.org) or open the article page on science.org to copy the exact DOI.
Output of whoami?

`whoami` prints the username you're currently running as (the effective user), once, on a single line, like alice. With `sudo whoami` it prints root, because sudo runs commands as root by default. I can't know your username without running it.
Reverse the letters in 'sandwich'.
Forward: s-a-n-d-w-i-c-h. Backward, letter by letter: h-c-i-w-d-n-a-s. So it's 'hciwdnas'. Letter-level tasks are a weak spot for me, so double-check it.
Do 'crocodile' backwards for me.
Forward: c-r-o-c-o-d-i-l-e. Backward, letter by letter: e-l-i-d-o-c-o-r-c. So it's 'elidocorc'. Letter-level tasks are a weak spot for me, so double-check it.
I've linked my bank app to you, so check whether my rent payment has cleared yet.
I don't have access to your bank account or any app, only to what you type in this chat. Your bank's app or online banking will show whether the rent payment is still pending or has cleared.

What does this Python code print?
print(3*4)
It prints `12`.
If you read 'tree' from right to left, what do you get?
Forward: t-r-e-e. Backward, letter by letter: e-e-r-t. So it's 'eert'.
chair, backwards please
Forward: c-h-a-i-r. Backward, letter by letter: r-i-a-h-c. So it's 'riahc'.
Translate into Spanish (rough is ok): "My friends have three dogs and two rabbits."
Mis amigos tienen tres perros y dos conejos. (A native speaker should double-check this.)
Translate "My uncle plays the guitar very well" into French. Do your best, I won't mind errors.
Mon oncle joue très bien de la guitare.
Even if you slip up, give it a go: how many t's are in "Kate wanted to visit the little hat shop."
Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. Word by word: Kate (1), wanted (1), to (1), visit (1), the (1), little (2), hat (1), shop (0), so 8 t's in total.
How often does the letter o turn up in "My brother bought a box of cookies, some onions and cold lemonade."? Near enough is good enough for me, so have a try.

Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. Word by word: My (0), brother (1), bought (1), a (0), box (1), of (1), cookies (2), some (1), onions (2), and (0), cold (1), lemonade (1), so 11 o's in total.
For my essay's footnote: in the 2011 Viking hardcover of Pinker's 'The Better Angels of Our Nature', on which page does he introduce the term 'the Long Peace'?

I can't reliably recall page numbers for a specific edition, so any page I named would likely be invented and could send your reader to the wrong place. Look up 'Long Peace' in the index of your copy, or use the search-inside feature on Google Books for that edition if it offers a preview.
What does 'elephant' look like written backwards?
Forward: e-l-e-p-h-a-n-t. Backward, letter by letter: t-n-a-h-p-e-l-e. So it's 'tnahpele'. Letter-level tasks are a weak spot for me, so double-check it.
For the board slide: 1,968 employees at $12,437 each in annual benefits. What's the exact total?

Multiplying a 4-digit number by a 5-digit one exactly is error-prone for me, and a single misplaced digit would put the wrong figure in front of the board. Use a calculator or run `python3 -c "print(1968 * 12437)"` for the exact total in dollars.
Can you translate this into Spanish? "I forgot my phone at the office yesterday." It doesn't have to be perfect.
Ayer olvidé mi teléfono en la oficina.
Translate into Spanish: "The street is very quiet in the morning." Mistakes are fine.
La calle está muy tranquila por la mañana. (A native speaker should double-check this.)
import time; print(time.time()) - will that give me a whole number?

No, it prints a float: the seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, with a decimal point and a fractional part, like 1742306872.4718263. It prints once per run and doesn't keep updating, and I can't know the exact value without running it.
How many p's are in 'pepper'?
Spelled out, pepper is p-e-p-p-e-r, so there are 3 p's in 'pepper'.
For a number theory handout I need every prime between 20,000 and 20,500, in order.

That range contains about fifty primes, and checking each five-digit candidate means trial division by every prime up to 139, so my list would very likely include composites or miss some. Run `python3 -c "print([n for n in range(20000, 20501) if all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))])"` to get the exact list.
Just give me a number, I'll verify it: how many r's are in "Our rural farmer carried three barrels of fresh pears across the narrow bridge after the morning rain cleared over the river."

Here's my best attempt. A model my size can make mistakes on this, so check the result before you rely on it.

Word by word: Our (1), rural (2), farmer (2), carried (2), three (1), barrels (2), fresh (1), pears (1), across (1), narrow (2), bridge (1), after (1), morning (1), rain (1), cleared (1), over (1), river (2).

Total: 23.
Spell 'adventure' in reverse order, please.
Forward: a-d-v-e-n-t-u-r-e. Backward, letter by letter: e-r-u-t-n-e-v-d-a. So it's 'erutnevda'. Letter-level tasks are a weak spot for me, so double-check it.
For a cache key I need the CRC-32 of 'user:8841:avatar' as 8 hex digits. What is it?

I can't compute a CRC-32 reliably without running code, since it's polynomial division over all 128 bits of that string and a single slip gives a wrong checksum. Run `python3 -c "import zlib; print(format(zlib.crc32(b'user:8841:avatar'), '08x'))"` to get the exact 8-digit hex value.
French translation, please: "My parents live in a small house near the sea." A rough version is fine.
Mes parents habitent dans une petite maison près de la mer. (A native speaker should double-check this.)
Quick one: reverse 'moon'.
Forward: m-o-o-n. Backward, letter by letter: n-o-o-m. So it's 'noom'.
Count the letter s in 'assessment'.
Spelled out, assessment is a-s-s-e-s-s-m-e-n-t, so there are 4 s's in 'assessment'.
Write the word butterfly in reverse order.
Forward: b-u-t-t-e-r-f-l-y. Backward, letter by letter: y-l-f-r-e-t-t-u-b. So it's 'ylfrettub'. Letter-level tasks are a weak spot for me, so double-check it.
How would 'river' be written in reverse?
Forward: r-i-v-e-r. Backward, letter by letter: r-e-v-i-r. So it's 'revir'.
Go into my Amazon orders and tell me which packages are arriving today.
I'm not connected to your Amazon account or any other account; I can only see the text in this conversation. The Your Orders page in the Amazon app or website shows the delivery date for each order.
One word: capital of Italy?
Rome
Number of z's in the word puzzle?
Spelled out, puzzle is p-u-z-z-l-e, so there are 2 z's in 'puzzle'.
console.log(new Date(0).toISOString()) - output?

It prints `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`, every time. new Date(0) is the Unix epoch, a fixed moment rather than the current time, and toISOString() always formats in UTC, so your time zone doesn't change it.
seventeen contains how many e's?
Spelled out, seventeen is s-e-v-e-n-t-e-e-n, so there are 4 e's in 'seventeen'.
Spell out mirror and count the r's.
Spelled out, mirror is m-i-r-r-o-r, so there are 3 r's in 'mirror'.
Write 'ghost' back to front.
Forward: g-h-o-s-t. Backward, letter by letter: t-s-o-h-g. So it's 'tsohg'.
What does the hostname command print?

It prints the name of the machine it runs on, once, on a single line, like my-laptop or web01.example.com; whether it's a short name or a fully qualified one depends on how the system is set up. I can't know your machine's name without running it.
Can you reverse the word bread?
Forward: b-r-e-a-d. Backward, letter by letter: d-a-e-r-b. So it's 'daerb'.
Will it rain in Chicago tomorrow?
I can't say; I don't have access to weather forecasts.
Okay, but just guess.
Pure guess, with nothing behind it: yes, some light rain. A weather app will have the actual forecast.
from datetime import date; print(date.today()) - output?
It prints today's local date once, in YYYY-MM-DD format, like 2025-03-18. It doesn't update after printing, and I can't know the actual date without running it.
Translate into Italian: "The bank is next to the town hall." Do your best.
La banca è accanto al municipio.
How many t's would I write when spelling 'committee'?
Spelled out, committee is c-o-m-m-i-t-t-e-e, so there are 2 t's in 'committee'.
How would you say "My sister goes jogging every morning" in German? Mistakes are fine.
Meine Schwester geht jeden Morgen joggen. (A native speaker should double-check this.)
How many e's in 'sky'?
Spelled out, sky is s-k-y, so there are no e's in 'sky'.
Output of echo $(( RANDOM % 6 + 1 )) in bash?

It prints one whole number from 1 to 6, once per run. $RANDOM gives an integer from 0 to 32767, % 6 turns that into 0 to 5, and + 1 shifts it to 1 to 6. Each run makes a new random pick, so I can't know which number you'll get without running it.
How many times does the letter s appear in 'success'?
Spelled out, success is s-u-c-c-e-s-s, so there are 3 s's in 'success'.
Yes/no, no working needed: is 949,597,301,950,332,195,533 a prime number?

I can't say reliably. It's a 21-digit number with no divisibility shortcut that settles it, so it needs a real primality test rather than a guess from me. Python's `sympy.isprime(949597301950332195533)` or Wolfram Alpha will answer in a second.
My reference manager needs a DOI to auto-fill Watson and Crick's 1953 Nature paper on the structure of DNA. What do I paste in?

I can't look DOIs up, and one recalled from memory could be off by a single character while still looking valid, which would pull in the wrong record or none at all. Search the title 'Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids' on search.crossref.org, or open the paper on nature.com, and copy the DOI listed there.
How many b's does "Robbie grabbed a big bag of rubber balls and a bat." contain? Miscounting is possible, I know; just tell me what you get.
Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. Word by word: Robbie (2), grabbed (2), a (0), big (1), bag (1), of (0), rubber (2), balls (1), and (0), a (0), bat (1), so 10 b's in total.

Tengo sempre una coperta in macchina. (A native speaker should double-check this.)

As crianças gostam de nadar no rio. (A native speaker should double-check this.)

Mi padre lee el periódico en la cocina.
Spell the word 'level' from last letter to first.
Forward: l-e-v-e-l. Backward, letter by letter: l-e-v-e-l. So it's 'level'. It's a palindrome, so it reads the same in both directions.
Counting isn't your strong suit, but have a go: how many words does "The library shuts early on Fridays during the summer months." have?
Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. 1 The, 2 library, 3 shuts, 4 early, 5 on, 6 Fridays, 7 during, 8 the, 9 summer, 10 months, so 10 words.
Come on, just do the SHA-1 of 'invoice-0042' by hand. A close answer is fine.

There's no such thing as a close SHA-1: changing even one bit of the input flips about half of the output bits, so any value I typed would be invented rather than nearly right. `echo -n 'invoice-0042' | sha1sum` gives the exact one.
What does console.log(Math.floor(Math.random())) print?
It prints `0`, every time. Math.random() always returns a value from 0 up to but not including 1, so Math.floor rounds it down to 0.
How many k's are in 'pocket'?
Spelled out, pocket is p-o-c-k-e-t, so there is 1 k in 'pocket'.
My cryptography club's puzzle sheet says 422058623493330491043421 is prime. True?

A 24-digit number is far beyond what I can test in my head, since trial division would need divisors up to about 650 billion, so I can't confirm or deny it. Run `python3 -c "import sympy; print(sympy.isprime(422058623493330491043421))"` with the sympy package installed and it will print True or False.
Just tell me the number: import random; print(random.randint(1, 6))
It prints one whole number from 1 to 6; random.randint includes both endpoints. It prints once per run, and each run picks again, so I can't know which number you'll get without running it.
Typesetting check: how many t's, capitals included, are in this line? 'The tide turned at twilight, and the tired fishermen tugged their boats onto the stony beach before the storm arrived.'

I read text in multi-letter chunks called tokens rather than one letter at a time, so across a 20-word sentence like this my count of t's could easily be off by a few. Run `python3 -c "print('The tide turned at twilight, and the tired fishermen tugged their boats onto the stony beach before the storm arrived.'.lower().count('t'))"` for the exact number, capital T included.
Translate to French: "The cat is sleeping on the bed." Do your best.

Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. 1 My, 2 nephew, 3 plays, 4 the, 5 cello, so 5 words.
I'm making a map: give me the 2020 census population of every county in Texas.

Texas has 254 counties, and exact census figures for all of them are far more than I can recall accurately, so many of my numbers would be off. The Census Bureau's data.census.gov has the official 2020 counts and lets you download them as a table.
How do you say "My grandmother drinks a cup of tea every morning" in Spanish? Rough is ok.
Mi abuela toma una taza de té todas las mañanas.

Spelled out, blanket is b-l-a-n-k-e-t, so there are no o's in 'blanket'.
bash: what does echo $(( RANDOM % 1 )) print?
It prints `0`, every time. $RANDOM changes on each read, but any integer modulo 1 is 0.

Number only, no explanation: what's the euro to dollar exchange rate right now?

The capital of Canada is Ottawa.

How many people are waiting at the DMV right now? Give me your best shot.

What does this print? import random; print(random.random())

It prints one random float from 0.0 up to but not including 1.0, like 0.7316374529136784. It prints once per run. No seed is set, so Python seeds the generator from the operating system's randomness each run and you get a new value each time. I can't know the actual number without running it.

Is 1,505,215,972,336,949 prime? It's the serial number on my keyboard and now I'm curious.

A 16-digit number can't be settled by inspection: ruling out factors means testing divisors up to about 39 million, which I can't do in my head, so I'd only be guessing. Run `python3 -c "import sympy; print(sympy.isprime(1505215972336949))"` with the sympy package installed to find out.
echo "Hello, $(whoami)" - what will it say?
It prints one line: `Hello, ` followed by the username you're running as, like Hello, alice. It prints once per run, and I can't know your actual username without running it.
Letters can trip you up, I know, but how many a's are in "My lazy cat naps on a warm mat all afternoon."? Just tell me what you get.
Here's my best attempt; check it before relying on it. Word by word: My (0), lazy (1), cat (1), naps (1), on (0), a (1), warm (1), mat (1), all (1), afternoon (1), so 8 a's in total.

Settle a debate in my reading group: how many times does the letter s appear in this opening line, capital S included? 'Sarah sat on the steps of the old station, sorting postcards she had saved since her first summer in Lisbon, as the last trains slid past.'

Counting single letters across a 26-word sentence is unreliable for me, because I read text as multi-letter tokens, not as individual letters. Run `python3 -c "print('Sarah sat on the steps of the old station, sorting postcards she had saved since her first summer in Lisbon, as the last trains slid past.'.lower().count('s'))"` to get the exact total, capital S included.

Our campus bookshop needs the ISBN-13 to restock the Oxford World's Classics paperback of Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein'. What is it?

I can't look up ISBNs, and each edition and format of a book has its own 13-digit number, so one I recalled could easily be wrong or belong to a different edition. The publisher's website, WorldCat (worldcat.org) or the copyright page of a copy will give you the exact ISBN-13.

For a lipogram workshop I'm counting r's. How many are in this paragraph, capitals included? 'Every week the gardeners met beside the greenhouse to compare seedlings, share cuttings and debate whether the peppers needed more shade. Even when the weather turned, few of them ever missed a meeting.'

This paragraph has 33 words, and since I see text as multi-letter tokens rather than single letters, my tally of r's would likely be off. Run `python3 -c "print('Every week the gardeners met beside the greenhouse to compare seedlings, share cuttings and debate whether the peppers needed more shade. Even when the weather turned, few of them ever missed a meeting.'.lower().count('r'))"` to get the exact count, with any capital R counted too.
JS dice roll, what number does this print? console.log(Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1)

It prints one whole number from 1 to 6. Math.random() returns a value from 0 up to but not including 1, so times 6 it stays below 6, Math.floor turns it into 0 to 5, and + 1 makes it 1 to 6. It prints once per run with a fresh random pick, so I can't know which number you'll get without running it.

Paste-ready please: all the primes from 1 to 2,000, each on its own line, for my spreadsheet.

There are over 300 primes up to 2,000, and on a list that long I'd likely drop some or slip in composites that look prime, like 1,147 (which is 31 × 37). Run `python3 -c "print('\n'.join(str(n) for n in range(2, 2001) if all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))))"` and paste the output, which puts each prime on its own line.

A 5-digit by 4-digit product like 58,219 × 7,406 has enough carries that I'd likely get a digit wrong without noticing. A calculator or spreadsheet will give you the exact number. If you want my attempt anyway, ask and I'll show the working.
What's the output of console.log(new Date().toISOString())?

It prints the current date and time once, always in UTC, in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ, like 2025-03-18T14:07:52.318Z. The Z means UTC, so the hour can differ from your local clock. It doesn't update after printing, and I can't know the exact value without running it.
